sources.entry: pydub - Manipulate audio with a simple and easy, high-level interface.

summary.one_liner: Pydub is a Python library for high-level audio manipulation, such as slicing, joining, volume and fade changes, crossfades, and format conversion through ffmpeg/libav.
summary.what_it_does: Pydub loads audio from WAV files natively and from other formats (mp3, ogg, flv, mp4, wma, aac, and anything else ffmpeg supports) through ffmpeg or libav. AudioSegment objects can be sliced by milliseconds, concatenated with +, repeated with *, and adjusted in volume with + or - decibel values. It supports crossfading via append, fade_in and fade_out, reversing, and reporting duration. Audio is exported to any ffmpeg-supported format with optional bitrate, tags, and raw ffmpeg parameters. A playback helper can play segments through simpleaudio, pyaudio, ffplay, or avplay.
use_cases: convert mp3, mp4, or flv files to mp3
slice and trim audio clips by time
crossfade and join songs into a playlist or mashup
adjust volume or fade in and out of audio
add metadata tags when exporting audio
batch process a folder of audio or video files
how_to_run: Install ffmpeg or libav (e.g. brew install ffmpeg, apt-get install ffmpeg libavcodec-extra, or the Windows binaries) and add it to PATH
stack: ffmpeg or libav (external binary, required for non-WAV formats)
optional playback: simpleaudio, pyaudio, ffplay, avplay
notable: Simple millisecond-based slicing, concatenation, and volume operations on an immutable AudioSegment object
Crossfade support through append with a crossfade duration
Export accepts tags, bitrate, and raw ffmpeg parameters
Built-in debug logger (pydub.converter) prints the ffmpeg subprocess calls
WAV read and write works in pure Python without ffmpeg
caveats: Non-WAV formats require ffmpeg or libav to be installed separately
Extra parameters passed to ffmpeg are not validated and depend on the local build
Playback needs one of several optional backends installed
